text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired -> HIGH: eu-west AZ1 capacity pressure / inference-serving queue growth / 503s starting
incident-bot: Alert details: service=redwood-inference-serving, group=eu-west, zone=eu-west-1a, symptom=tokenize/serve latency spike > 2s, error_rate=7.8%, inferred_cause=instance OOM / degraded autoscale
oncall-ana: acked oncall. I'm on it. Paging SRE now. :rotating_light:
sre-jamie: I'm awake, joining. Pulling metrics and logs now. Which customers are impacted?
support-lee: Saw 3 tickets from Xero-Partner and one internal 500 from playground. Customer-facing errors show 503/timeout. I can surface to CS.
eng-runtime-ryan: adding context — we rolled a kernel/quantization tweak to eu-west yesterday (canary) but only to dedicated pools. Monitoring if rollout overlapped AZ1 nodes.
oncall-ana: timeline: spike started ~1713001200 (approx). Autoscale didn't bring up nodes in AZ1; queue depth increased. Trying manual scale in the AZ now.
oncall-ana: running command to list instance health:
```
infra-ctl list-instances --region eu-west --zone eu-west-1a --filter status!=healthy
```
oncall-ana: 6/12 instances reporting unhealthy, memory pressure, one OOM kill in logs. Nodedump attached in ops.
sre-jamie: I’m SSHing into a failed node. Kernel shows repeated OOM killer on java process (kv-cache). Looks like prefix cache grew unexpectedly.
eng-runtime-ryan: hmm kv-cache growth — did we accidentally enable longer max-context in routing? Checking rollout config.
eng-runtime-ryan: searching git for last deploy: `git rev-parse --short HEAD` -> 0a7f9d3. Deploy checksum matches yesterday canary but shouldn't be global.
incident-bot: incident severity set to P1 by oncall-ana due to customer errors and increased error rate
oncall-ana: immediate mitigation plan:
- step1: divert new inference traffic away from eu-west-1a to eu-west-1b/c (failover routing)
- step2: scale down affected pool to prevent repeated OOM and restart runtime with kv-cache cap
- step3: enable temporary quota on long-context requests
- step4: notify customers and CS
sre-jamie: executing failover route change now (will update DNS/routing policy)
sre-jamie: command:
```
router-ctl set-weight --region eu-west --zone eu-west-1a 0 --reason "emerg failover"
router-ctl set-weight --region eu-west --zone eu-west-1b 50
router-ctl set-weight --region eu-west --zone eu-west-1c 50
```
support-lee: FYI sending a templated status msg to affected customers: "We're seeing elevated errors in eu-west AZ1 and routing traffic away while we investigate. No data loss; service is available in other AZs."
product-kate: please include estimated ETA for full restore in the msg if we have one. CS wants to set expectations.
oncall-ana: ETA preliminary 30-45m for full stabilization after failover; manual node restarts + cache cap required. Will update when scaled and health green.
eng-runtime-ryan: patch to runtime to enforce kv-cache soft cap queued; pushing a safe restart to affected nodes once traffic is off AZ1. Patch diff:
```
- kv_cache.max_entries = 5000000
+ kv_cache.max_entries = 500000
```
sre-jamie: scaling down and restarting pods in AZ1 now. Using rolling restart to avoid further OOM cascades.
oncall-ana: monitoring metrics: queue depth decreasing in eu-west overall, 503s dropping from 7.8% -> 2.1% in last 90s. Good sign.
incident-bot: escalation: paging infra-ops-bot for potential instance replacement if restarts don't recover
infra-ops-bot: spawned replacement instances in eu-west-1a; new instances are joining the pool but held in standby until we validate runtime config.
oncall-ana: after failover, observed small spike in latency in eu-west-1b as shard warmed caches; within SLOs but visible.
support-lee: CS updated customers with ETA and note about failover; flagged highest-severity accounts for direct outreach.
eng-runtime-ryan: rolling in kv-cache cap patch to AZ1 nodes now. After restart, will run a short synthetic workload to validate stability.
sre-jamie: restarted runtime on 4 affected nodes, memory pressure cleared on 3, one node still OOMing — taking that node out of pool.
oncall-ana: taking node out with command:
```
infra-ctl drain-instance i-0a12b3 --region eu-west --zone eu-west-1a
```
oncall-ana: health across EU region shows CPU/memory normalized, error rate ~0.9% now. Queue depth back to baseline.
product-kate: how many customers saw errors? we need a short impact summary for post-incident comms.
support-lee: preliminary: ~12 tenants had retried requests with visible 5xxs (mostly short-lived). No data corruption. Two SDK clients reported degraded latency >5s for a minute.
oncall-ana: action log for P1:
- failover routing executed at 1713001302
- kv-cache cap patch applied to AZ1 nodes and restarted at 1713001500
- unhealthy nodes drained/replaced and pool recovered by 1713002600
- customer notifications sent at 1713001400
- incident severity set P1 and will be reviewed for postmortem
sre-jamie: doing a quick hypothesis: a local autoscale race + unchecked kv-cache growth triggered memory exhaustion on AZ1. Need follow-ups: autoscaler retry/timeout tuning, kv-cache soft limits, and rollout gating for runtime patches.
eng-runtime-ryan: agree. I'll open a follow-up PR to add a runtime feature-flag gating and autoscaler backoff. Also add canary variance to prevent cross-AZ bleed.
incident-bot: escalation closed (no active oncall escalations). Incident still P1 until we finish impact review.
oncall-ana: handing off to oncall for next shift (sre-jamie remains on follow-ups). Handoff note: monitor eu-west error rate, ensure no flapping nodes, and verify post-incident regression tests.
sre-jamie: taking ownership for follow-up items. I'll schedule a postmortem doc and link to config diffs.
product-kate: thanks — once postmortem ready, we'll coordinate customer-facing summary and internal postmortem review.
oncall-ana: marking incident mitigated at 1713003034. Will keep thread for final notes.
incident-bot: Incident mitigated flag set. Please fill out incident form at https://redwood.ops/incidents/1713001234
sre-jamie: filing ticket RFC-231 for autoscaler tuning and runtime kv-cap. Assigning to eng-runtime.
support-lee: closing customer tickets as we confirm stability; will reopen if issues resurface.
oncall-ana: final note: no evidence of config rollback; root cause likely combination of kv-cache growth + az-specific instance pool fragmentation. Full timeline and action owners in postmortem.
